audit.whatIsWrong: The whole matchup is built on 'her E blink' — the escape you must bait, ground and count. It is not her E. It is her W, Across the Veil. The content layer never names a single Aurora ability, and the full layer writes the name as 'Across the Veil (Hop)'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Across the Veil (W) is 'Aurora leaps in a direction of her choosing, entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible, and gaining Move Speed' on 22/21/20/19/18s. Her E, The Weirding, is a damage-and-slow blast on 15/14/13/12/11s that hops her backward afterwards. Calling the escape 'E' points the player at the wrong cooldown by seven seconds and at the wrong ability entirely — you bait and count a 22s leap, not a 15s poke tool. Also missing: Spirit Abjuration (P) heals Aurora off her spells and attacks, which is why Grievous Wounds decides the two-item duel.
audit.corrected: Every reference to the blink renamed to Across the Veil with its 22s rank-1 cooldown; The Weirding named where the backward hop is meant; Spirit Abjuration and anti-heal added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart says Cassiopeia owns Level 3 through First item while every one of its own whys for those stages says Aurora does.
audit.why: whys[2] says 'the DPS treadmill exists but can't catch her this early', whys[3] says Aurora 'keeps renting you the lane at a markup', whys[4] says Petrifying Gaze can't catch her, whys[5] says her first item 'can delete you'. The early and mid prose agree: 'Levels 1 to 3 are hers', 'Levels 4 to 6 are still uphill'. Only the two-item stage is Cassiopeia's, which the late text states outright. The prose is internally consistent and the chart is the outlier, so the chart moves.
audit.corrected: win[0..5]=Aurora, win[6]=Cassiopeia, with the full-layer phase sides matched to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears for Across the Veil anywhere, even though 'bait it, count it, then go' is repeated in four places.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s and Between Worlds is 140/120/100s. The 22s number is the single most actionable fact in the matchup because the entire Cassiopeia game plan is to commit inside that window.
audit.corrected: 22s at rank 1 now stated in the win condition, the cooldown block, the do's, the mid and late text and the all-in windows.

audit.why: 67.82% over 87 games at Emerald+ with a level chart that hands Aurora six of seven lane stages is not a contradiction — it is a scaling matchup. Cassiopeia loses the lane cheaply and wins the game from two items on, which is exactly what the late text says. I set the chart to the prose rather than to the win rate for that reason.

edits.before: Levels 1 to 3 are hers and you have to respect it — Aurora's Q poke and W spirit both out-range my Noxious Blast (Q), and until my poison engine exists I'm just a slow caster eating harass. Don't throw a Q she can sidestep and then punish; last-hit at the tip of my Q, take the chip, and only start stacking poison when she steps up to CS. My one trump is W Miasma — the instant she dashes in I drop the ground cloud on her landing spot to lock the blink and disable her E, but pre-6 I'm baiting that escape, not all-inning.
edits.after: Levels 1 to 3 are hers and I have to respect it — Aurora's Twofold Hex and her spirit poke both out-range my Noxious Blast (Q), and until my poison engine exists I'm just a slow caster eating harass. My one trump is W Miasma — the instant she commits I drop the ground cloud on her landing spot to lock Across the Veil, but pre-6 I'm baiting that 22s leap, not all-inning.

edits.before: Levels 4 to 6 are still uphill: she has the range and the burst, and even my ult doesn't fix it. Petrifying Gaze (R) wants a face-check, but Aurora just ults the cone and blinks the stun with her E, then resets — so I don't gamble my one hard-CD on catching her. I farm, I poke back with Q when she over-extends, and I prime her with Q or W so my Twin Fang (E) refunds its cooldown and chains. The plan is to lose this phase as cheaply as possible and bank every plate I deny and every blink I track for the 2-item window.

edits.before: This is where I take the lane back, and it's why we're FAVOURED overall. With two items, my passive bonus move speed (I never buy boots) plus the speed burst off Q-on-hit let me run her down between blinks, and my poison-into-Twin-Fang chain out-DPSes her burst in any exchange longer than her cooldowns. The kill pattern is fixed: track her E, drop W Miasma to ground her the instant the blink is gone, then chain Twin Fang on her squishy frame while she's stuck in my poison. She still bursts me if I face-tank her root combo with no resists — so I never walk in until that blink is down.
